--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_random_regular_expander_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add a random d-regular graph that is guaranteed to be a (nearly) Ramanujan expander. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_random_regular_expander_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add a random d-regular graph that is guaranteed to be a (nearly) Ramanujan expander. title: >- [Graph.add_random_regular_expander_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a random d-regular graph that is guaranteed to be a (nearly) Ramanujan expander. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a random `d`-regular graph that is guaranteed to be a (nearly) Ramanujan expander. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19958-L20100){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_random_regular_expander_graph( n, d, epsilon=0.0, max_tries=100, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random regular expander graph](../assets/graphs/add-random-regular-expander-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random regular expanders on a ring of nine nodes for d=2, 4, and 6. Candidates are built like the maybe-regular expander and kept only once their second eigenvalue meets the Ramanujan bound, so each graph is d-regular and a proven expander: a nine-cycle in shuffled order, then 18 and 27 edges." width="100%"} Builds candidates like `add_maybe_regular_expander()`, as the union of `d / 2` edge-disjoint random Hamiltonian cycles on `n` nodes, and keeps the first one whose second-largest adjacency eigenvalue (in absolute value) is below `2 sqrt(d - 1) + epsilon`. With `epsilon=0` that is the Ramanujan bound, the best spectral gap a large `d`-regular graph can have, so the result mixes random walks and spreads information about as fast as possible for its degree. Most candidates pass, so few retries are needed. It is NetworkX's `random_regular_expander_graph()`. Each test computes all `n` eigenvalues, which takes time proportional to `n^3`, so the method suits graphs of up to a few thousand nodes. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random regular expanders are useful for: - sparse networks with provably fast mixing, for gossip, load balancing and peer-to-peer overlays - benchmarks for spectral and random-walk algorithms - building blocks of pseudo-random constructions and error-correcting codes ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be positive and at least `d + 1`. [d]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degree of every node: an even number, at least `2`. [epsilon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Slack added to the Ramanujan bound `2 sqrt(d - 1)`. Default is `0`. Must be non-negative. [max_tries]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How many candidates to test, and how many times each cycle may be redrawn, before giving up. Default is `100`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is not positive, `d=` is odd or less than `2`, `n - 1` is less than `d=`, `epsilon=` is negative, or no candidate passes in `max_tries=` attempts. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_maybe_regular_expander`) : Build a regular graph from Hamiltonian cycles, unchecked. [](`~add_random_regular_graph`) : Draw a uniform random regular graph. [](`~is_regular_expander`) : Check the spectral expansion of a regular graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 6-regular expander on 100 nodes: ::: {#6cbd1e60 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_random_regular_expander_graph(n=100, d=6, seed=2) graph.count_edges(), graph.is_regular_expander() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (300, True) ``` ::: ::: Its small diameter reflects the expansion: ::: {#70e104d2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5 ``` ::: ::: ### Random or local edges Two 4-regular graphs on `30` nodes, with the nodes in order around a circle. On the left, the expander's edges jump all over the circle. On the right, the ring lattice from `add_smallworld_graph()` with `p=0.0` joins each node only to the two nodes on either side, so it takes twice as many steps to cross and fails the expander check: ::: {#0b62c9b6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} expander = ec.Graph().add_random_regular_expander_graph(n=30, d=4, seed=1) ring = ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=30, k=4, p=0.0) [(g.diameter(), g.is_regular_expander()) for g in (expander, ring)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [(4, True), (8, False)] ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#6bae6636 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} expander.layout_circular(order="id").plot( layout="pos", show_labels=False, node_size=6, width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
